mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up stock prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests a weakening labor market, which could lead to reduced consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate rises above 5%, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment increases but the unemployment rate does not decrease, it may indicate inefficiencies in the labor market that could lead to economic stagnation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Payroll employment increases without a corresponding decrease in the unemployment rate, but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A high and rising federal funds rate indicates a tightening monetary policy, which can lead to reduced borrowing and spending, negatively impacting economic growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The federal funds rate is high and rising, but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the 60-day horizon in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests strong economic activity, which should positively impact corporate revenues and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production increases, but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPI) indicates inflationary pressures, which could lead to tighter monetary policy and negative impacts on equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The CPI increases by more than 3% annualized, but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence between housing starts and retail sales suggests an imbalance in economic activity, which could lead to reduced consumer confidence and negative impacts on equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts and retail sales diverge, but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate combined with high industrial production suggests a late-stage economic expansion, which could lead to increased equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate is low and industrial production is high, but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
